kingdoms.name: Amberfall
kingdoms.public_account: Most Amberfolk know the black rot as contradictory carriage talk: poisoned rain, a Draznan civil war, bad grain, or an eastern superstition. Oakrun has stains and sick roots, but no authority has named them.
kingdoms.travel_motive: The warm western roads still promise food, work, replacement horses, and a bed. They also funnel anyone seeking Drazna through Oakrun, where every version of the eastern disaster meets.
kingdoms.character: A pastoral crown of hedged fields, orchard shires, practical market towns, and a distant monarchy that is felt chiefly through roads and stamped coin.

kingdoms.name: The Draznan Crown
kingdoms.public_account: Drazna holds the oldest widely verified account of black water spoiling stone, roots, flesh, and names. That makes it the first recorded kingdom, not a proven birthplace. The distinction is usually lost before a rumor reaches Oakrun.
kingdoms.travel_motive: Survivors go home for missing kin; physicians and opportunists go for samples; clerks go for dates; frightened pilgrims go because every other account points east. The same traffic carries distorted testimony back out.
kingdoms.character: A lake crown rebuilt vertically after old floods: wet timber wards, slate roofs, sluice galleries, ferries, memorial archives, and inhabited bridges over the drowned city.

kingdoms.name: Rouvray
kingdoms.public_account: Rouvrain hospices receive Draznan refugees and blackened cargo. Cathedral authorities call the corruption a material contagion while roadside preachers call it judgment; both stories produce fires at the gates.
kingdoms.travel_motive: Its hospitals, scriptoria, and guarded pilgrim roads draw the injured and the curious. Its southern field road is the long alternative when the direct Draznan causeway becomes impassable.
kingdoms.character: A country of limestone cathedral towns, bell roads, chalk fields, vineyards, charitable hospices, and increasingly severe gate inspections.

locations.name: Oakrun Crossroads
locations.description: A great oak, a warm inn, a stable yard, and the meeting of the south road with older ways whose stones disagree with modern maps.

locations.name: Oakrun North Road
locations.description: A rutted approach where horses shy before travellers see any threat and black mud clings beneath ordinary brown clay.

locations.name: Oakrun Orchard Lane
locations.description: Maud Bell's worked rows, cider press, and pale treated roots lie along a buried watercourse.

locations.name: Oakrun Old Mill Yard
locations.description: The stopped mill stands above sweet-smelling black silt and a track recently widened for a narrow wagon.

locations.name: Oakrun Pilgrim's Hollow
locations.description: A roofed roadside hollow where stranded travellers sleep beside worn stones that still point east.

locations.name: Oakrun Old Tollhouse
locations.description: Fen Alder inhabits the ruined counting post among wheel marks, duplicate tallies, and the remains of an abolished route.

locations.name: Oakrun Barrow Verge
locations.description: Crowned stones and disturbed graves overlook the north road; tally-keepers were buried here before the toll moved.

locations.name: Oakrun Severed Fieldsite
locations.description: Broken apparatus and blackened holding pits occupy a cut in the fields beyond the abandoned mill.

locations.name: Alderwick
locations.description: Amberfall's low brick capital surrounds a broad coach yard, wool market, river stairs, and crown offices that receive eastern reports weeks late.

locations.name: The Briarwash Fields
locations.description: Miles of sheep pasture and drainage ditches make a visible but exposed approach to the capital.

locations.name: Hollowmere Post
locations.description: The last Amberfall toll shed faces a flooded eastern mile. Drivers wait here to join convoys or quietly turn around.

locations.name: Drazna, High Crown
locations.description: The surviving palace height commands sluices, bridges, and the drowned foundations of Old Drazna without controlling all of them.

locations.name: Drazna, Lantern Quays
locations.description: Ferries, eel smoke, salvage stalls, and refugee notices crowd the lowest inhabited quay above black-marked pilings.

locations.name: Drazna, Birch Heights
locations.description: The House of Names keeps flood tablets and household rolls on a dry slope planted with white birch.

locations.name: Drazna, Crown Sluice
locations.description: Timber gears, water gauges, pressure galleries, and sealed lower channels keep the surviving wards above the lake.

locations.name: Drazna, Walking Ward
locations.description: Black-timber homes and workshops bridge from roof to roof where streets have become canals.

locations.name: Drazna, Undertide
locations.description: Dry docks and drowned service passages appear only as the lake falls. Divers, smugglers, and wardens all claim different maps.

locations.name: Bellifont
locations.description: Rouvray's limestone capital grows around a cathedral close, physic gardens, crowded hospices, and gate yards bright with inspection fires.

locations.name: Saint Orée Hospice
locations.description: A road hospital outside Bellifont where Draznan arrivals are washed, named, questioned, and sometimes refused entry.

locations.name: The Orison Fields
locations.description: Chalk roads cross vineyard walls and open grain country where travellers can see danger long before they can escape it.

locations.name: Hollow Bells Post
locations.description: A wind-cut gate below the pass hangs cracked bells for each missing coach. No keeper agrees what rings them at night.

routes.name: The Near North Road
routes.description: A short, familiar road whose horses have recently begun to fear the last bend.

routes.name: Orchard Lane
routes.description: A worked lane between hedges, irrigation ditches, and Maud's cider rows.

routes.name: The Pilgrim Spur
routes.description: A worn western spur preserved because travellers still sleep beneath its little roof.

routes.name: The Abolished Toll
routes.description: Weeds obscure the wheel ruts, but Fen still counts every axle that passes.

routes.name: Tally-Keeper's Rise
routes.description: The road climbs among crown stones and graves older than the current toll.

routes.name: The Worn-Saint Cut
routes.description: A steep cut allows careful travellers to avoid returning by the north bend.

routes.name: Millwater Lane
routes.description: The buried watercourse becomes visible beside roots that no longer smell alive.

routes.name: The Severed Track
routes.description: Recent wagon work has reopened a track through long grass to the broken holding site.

routes.name: The Counting Ditch
routes.description: A drainage ditch and service road close Oakrun's northern loop.

routes.name: The Amberfall Highroad
routes.description: The dependable south road crosses the Briarwash grazing country before reaching Alderwick's coach yard.

routes.name: The Wool Road
routes.description: Shepherd tracks and crown milestones spread across the capital's near fields.

routes.name: The Unharvested Miles
routes.description: Abandoned strips of rye and blind hedges lead to the last eastern toll shed.

routes.name: The Glasswater Causeway
routes.description: Raised stones and drowned villages cross the lakeward marsh to Drazna. Some milestones are visible only at low water.

routes.name: The Lantern Climb
routes.description: Stone stairs and haul ramps climb from the quay to the palace height.

routes.name: Birch Stair
routes.description: A dry memorial road connects crown offices to the House of Names.

routes.name: The Gauge Walk
routes.description: A watched service walk follows pressure pipes and emergency spillways.

routes.name: The Walking Bridges
routes.description: Rope-braced bridges flex between inhabited roofs and quay cranes.

routes.name: The Low-Water Descent
routes.description: Mud stairs and old dock roofs emerge beneath the quay as the lake falls.

routes.name: The Pass of Hollow Bells
routes.description: A high coach road crosses rain-black ridges between Drazna and Rouvray.

routes.name: The Bell Road
routes.description: Limestone shrines and inspected waystations mark the descent toward Bellifont.

routes.name: Saint Orée Road
routes.description: A crowded gate road joins the capital's eastern ward to its refugee hospice.

routes.name: The Orison Road
routes.description: Vineyard walls and processional stones lead into open chalk country.

routes.name: The Long Penance
routes.description: A long southern alternative links Rouvray and Amberfall through exposed fields, toll chapels, and no reliable shelter.

hostile_passages.name: The Barrow Turn
hostile_passages.warning: Horses sweat white before the crowned stones become visible.
hostile_passages.description: Old tally-keepers leave their graves after sunset and follow wheels rather than footsteps.

hostile_passages.name: The Scentless Runoff
hostile_passages.warning: Birds stop at the last healthy ditch and the air loses the smell of wet soil.
hostile_passages.description: A narrow black seep crosses the lane upstream of Maud's press.

hostile_passages.name: The Fieldsite Cut
hostile_passages.warning: The grass lies outward from pits that look shallow until weight touches them.
hostile_passages.description: Escaped animals and unstable holding trenches make the reopened service road lethal.

hostile_passages.name: Briarwash Verge
hostile_passages.warning: Fresh-cut briar bundles appear beside milestones where no hedge work is due.
hostile_passages.description: A small reaver band taxes lone carts but avoids scheduled coaches with visible guards.

hostile_passages.name: The Unharvested Miles
hostile_passages.warning: Rye stands black at the base while its heads remain gold, and no farm smoke rises beyond it.
hostile_passages.description: Blind hedges conceal abandoned holdings, hungry animals, and people who now live by stopping eastbound traffic.

hostile_passages.name: The Black Mile
hostile_passages.warning: The causeway's white stones turn mirror-black one by one, and drowned doorframes stand in the reeds.
hostile_passages.description: Floodwater crosses broken stones above a drowned hamlet whose dead return to the road when wheels disturb the silt.

hostile_passages.name: Undertide Mouth
hostile_passages.warning: Divers chalk the safe waterline anew each morning; yesterday's marks end below the surface.
hostile_passages.description: The old dry-dock descent is accessible for hours at a time and never has the same hazards twice.

hostile_passages.name: Hollow Bells Pass
hostile_passages.warning: Cracked bells ring upslope in still air, followed by stones moving where no cart can be seen.
hostile_passages.description: Storm damage and abandoned military posts leave long blind climbs controlled by deserter camps.

hostile_passages.name: The Penitent Mile
hostile_passages.warning: Unlicensed shrines ask travellers to burn eastern possessions before they may pass.
hostile_passages.description: A moving camp of armed penitents controls wells along the most exposed section of the southern road.

carriages.name: The Oak and Crown
carriages.description: Hester's broad, well-maintained coach keeps Oakrun tied to Amberfall's capital and carries most reliable dated news.

carriages.name: The Grey Heron
carriages.description: A narrow, high-wheeled east coach that runs only when Jory can form a convoy at Hollowmere. It is not safe; it is merely still running.

carriages.name: The Bell and Reed
carriages.description: A long-bodied Rouvrain coach used by pilgrims, physicians, and families avoiding the Draznan road.

carriages.name: The Mudwheel
carriages.description: A small freight wagon that Lina uses to carry names, letters, and people uphill from arriving ferries.
